evidence.note: Candidate applies universal material/weather relations only; no local feature, state, route, resource or result.
Candidate applies husbandry and storage dependencies only; no household, animal, stock, ownership, access, yield or veterinary outcome.
Candidate applies general interference and clearance relations only; it is not a worksite inventory, safety code or repair procedure.
Candidate applies universal travel dependencies only; it creates no road, guide, safe passage, distance or arrival.
Candidate composition of already established people, equipment, animal, place and supply concerns. It creates no force, command, weapon, conflict, doctrine or combat outcome.
Candidate composition of existing writing, craft observation, possession and access boundaries. It creates no literacy, apprenticeship, title, permission, authority or legal result.
Candidate is non-diagnostic hygiene context only; it creates no sickness, contamination, helper, treatment, cleanliness, recovery or outcome.
Candidate applies established-input food/animal dependencies only; it creates no animal, food, product, safety, ration, yield or care result.

object.value: At an established place, drainage changes where water stands
ground bearing changes footing and load placement
vegetation can screen sight and snag a load
wind and wetness change exposure
daylight changes what can be inspected or done safely. Each relation requires the observed place and condition.
Dry stored grain needs protection from wetting and pests
fodder is kept apart from animal waste
animals need water, feed, shelter and routine handling
a yard needs a passable path for people and loads
cleaning or moving stock takes labour and interrupts other work. These depend on existing household, stock and stores.
A work flow needs a clear path between material, tool and work surface
a carried load can obstruct another task
heat, sparks and dry fuel need separation
moisture changes material handling and drying time
moving parts or suspended loads require people and loose clothing to stay clear. Actual equipment and conditions decide the result.
A wet or uneven surface changes footing and pace
darkness or poor visibility weakens wayfinding
wind, rain and cold increase exposure
a heavier load changes endurance and balance
tracks, landmarks and local knowledge can aid orientation but can be absent, old or misleading. This proves neither route nor arrival.
People on watch need relief, food, water and shelter according to actual circumstances
equipment needs carrying, storage and inspection
a horse needs fodder, water, rest and handling
damp can affect clothing, cords and stored supplies
a march or guard changes only through available routes, orders, people and material means. This supplies no force, command or combat result.
A written carrier can be copied, carried, read aloud or left unread according to access and literacy
learning a craft requires observation, instruction, practice and materials
requested entry or tool use remains subject to the holder's response
possession and ownership are not the same fact
a disputed object can prompt inquiry, return, refusal or appeal without fixing a legal outcome.
Cleaning hands, tools and contact surfaces removes visible soil but does not diagnose illness
separating waste from water and food reduces direct contact
rest, warmth and protection can support comfort after exertion or minor injury
a wound can be covered and observed for change
experienced help may be sought when available, without promised diagnosis or recovery.
Food can spoil when time, warmth and moisture favour deterioration
clean handling and separation from waste reduce direct fouling
an animal product needs an actual animal and collection or processing labour
animals need water, feed, rest and shelter appropriate to conditions
milk, meat, eggs, hides or wool are not interchangeable and each depends on a real source and handling path.
